rounds.fact: The Wall was a single editable text field in the earliest versions. 2007's platform launch brought app chaos, sheep-throwing included, before the News Feed took over the world.
Digital Trends grew as a general consumer-electronics review site during the mid-2000s, competing for readers alongside CNET and Engadget in a crowded gadget-blog era.
Napster's original file-sharing service was sued into shutting down in 2001, but the brand survived and was later relaunched as a legal paid streaming service.
Excite was one of the 'big five' web portals of the late 90s, and famously turned down the chance to buy Google's search technology for under $1 million in 1999.
Walmart's first e-commerce attempt in 2000 struggled so badly with web traffic that the company briefly shut the site down and rebuilt it before relaunching.
